text:
SRE-Bot: :red_circle: PGPU pool saturation detected — 429 spike on /v1/generate, tokenbucket rejects rising. paging ops-oncall@redwood

Ops Oncall (Jamie): on it. linking dashboards and start a thread. can someone confirm magnitude?

Mateo Rivera: seeing 429 rate jump to ~18% over last 6m, queue depth on hotpool G-1 at 4.2k, average latency for queued requests now 2.4s and rising.

Priya Kapoor: autoscaler logs show repeated failed scale attempts: "InstanceLaunchQuotaExceeded" from our cloud provider when trying to add more nodes to hotpool. scaling policy hit account cap.

Alice Chen: ugh. so autoscaler is trying but provider quota blocked it. that explains queue grow. any sign of cascading tokenbucket misconfig?

Mateo Rivera: yes — tokenbucket refill rates were rolled earlier today for per-tier defaults. I see many routes hitting per-route burst=0 effectively. 429s not just from full queues but immediate TB rejects pre-enqueue.

Ingrid (infra): checking the rollout: earlier patch changed tokenbucket.window from "1000" to "1s" and someone meant ms -> units mismatch. refill calculation uses window in seconds, so we dropped refill by 1000x. digging logs.

Priya Kapoor: can you paste the config diff?

Mateo Rivera: here — the bad snippet:

```
- tokenbucket:
-   capacity: 100
-   refill: 50
-   window: 1000   # intended ms
+ tokenbucket:
+   capacity: 100
+   refill: 50
+   window: 1s      # new change (but runtime expects seconds numeric)
```

Mateo Rivera: Runtime expects numeric seconds (float). the string "1s" got parsed as 1 => ok, but the earlier deploy used 1000 (ms) which runtime took as 1000s in a different path? there's inconsistent parsing between validator and runtime, leading to an effective refill rate that was orders of magnitude off. in short: unit mismatch across services.

Ops Oncall (Jamie): ok this matches: two problems: provider quota blocked autoscale (can't add capacity), and tokenbucket misconfig tightened throttles. both amplified user 429s. we need immediate mitigations: 1) open provider quota request / emergency increase 2) revert tokenbucket change to safe defaults 3) route critical customer traffic to fallback pools.

Alice Chen: I can push a targeted rollback for tokenbucket defaults to prod for the affected routes now. prepping patch. @deploy-bot can you stand by for canary?

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: roll back config tokenbucket-defaults -> canary to 3 nodes. approve with `/deploy approve 1954321000`

Priya Kapoor: while that deploy runs, I'm adding a temporary emergency throttle policy: lower capacity for free-tier routes to preserve capacity for enterprise-tier. policy applied at edge route router.

Mateo Rivera: careful — we should reduce free-tier tokens but not adjust paid tiers unless we know refill math. do not set refill=0.

Ingrid (infra): provider quota request submitted to cloud console (case #CLD-7812), reached out to account rep for emergency bump. ETA unknown ~30-60m typical. meanwhile we can split load: divert ~40% of paid-tier traffic to secondary pool in us-west-2 with warm nodes. starting warm-up of warmpool-b.
